answer: Part IV, Running the School, covers teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership. These chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members.

children.name: Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback
children.blurb: Fifteen teachers in five primary schools in England used AI to help plan lessons for two school terms. Their self reported weekly planning time fell by 52.5 percent, from about 10 hours to under 5 (Carson et al., 2026).

children.name: Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System
children.blurb: Researchers who build systems to predict student failure found something troubling when they looked closely. A single accuracy number made predictions look more reliable than they were.

children.name: Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance
children.blurb: Boston Public Schools once faced a transportation problem that cost more than $100 million a year. Researchers built an optimization system that redesigned the bus routes, saving about $5 million a year and removing 50 buses while keeping service quality (Bertsimas et al., 2019).

children.name: People, Leadership, and Culture
children.blurb: Researchers interviewed leaders in six Colorado school districts about how they first responded to AI. Some wrote informal guidelines, some banned student use, and some updated their acceptable use policies (McGuire et al., 2026).

sections.body: This section is about the daily work of running a school and a district, and it looks at how AI fits into that work as the book describes it. It covers teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership. These chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members. The book treats these as the last four chapters of the Volume, turning from earlier material to the practical running of a school.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book holds that this part of school life is where leadership decisions matter most, and it states its core argument in full in the final chapter. It sets out a plan for the first 90 days, then a short conclusion looks back at what the evidence shows and ahead to what may change. What works, what does not, and the rule the book holds to are given through these chapters rather than as a separate list. The rule it holds to is that these chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages fit together as the four areas of running a school, and each one serves a different reader. A teacher would go to Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback for the classroom side of planning and grading. A leader would go to Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System for assessment and data work, and to Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance for the operational and financial side. A principal or board member would go to People, Leadership, and Culture for the human and leadership side, and the final chapter then states the core argument and the first 90 days.
